questions.question: Which of the following features must be supported by any programming language to become a pure object-oriented programming language?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A pure object-oriented language must support encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism (along with abstraction), so more than one option is correct.

questions.question: Which collision resolution technique involves placing collided elements in the next available empty slot in the hash table?
questions.explanation: Linear probing resolves a collision by checking the next slots one by one (h+1, h+2, ...) until an empty one is found. Quadratic probing jumps by squares and double hashing uses a second hash function.

questions.question: Which concept allows a class to inherit properties and behaviors from multiple classes?
questions.explanation: Multiple inheritance is the specific form of inheritance in which one class derives from more than one base class. Plain 'Inheritance' is the general concept, not specifically from multiple classes.

questions.question: A threaded binary tree is a binary tree in which:

options.B: Each node has at most one child
options.C: Each node is connected to its parent
options.D: Each node has a thread connecting it to its predecessor or successor

questions.explanation: In a threaded binary tree the otherwise NULL left/right pointers are replaced by threads to the inorder predecessor or successor, enabling traversal without a stack. It does not require every node to have two children.

questions.question: In OOP, what does the term "method signature" refer to?

options.B: The return type of the method
options.D: The combination of method name and parameter types

questions.explanation: A method signature is the method name together with its parameter types (number, type and order). The return type is not part of the signature in Java/C++ overloading rules.

questions.question: An index is clustered, if

options.A: it is on a set of fields that form a candidate key.
options.B: it is on a set of fields that include the primary key.
options.C: the data records of the file are organized in the same order as the data entries of the index.
options.D: the data records of the file are organized not in the same order as the data entries of the index.

questions.explanation: An index is clustered when the data records are physically stored in the same order as the index's data entries. Being on a key or primary key does not by itself make an index clustered.

options.B: The program is compiled and executed successfully
options.C: The program gives a compile-time error
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Applying delete to a null pointer is defined in C++ as a no-op, so the program compiles and runs successfully. There is neither a compile-time error nor undefined behaviour.

questions.question: A PDA chooses the next move based on:
questions.explanation: A PDA's transition depends on the current state, the next input symbol (or epsilon) and the top-of-stack symbol. Since the stack top is not included, none of the options is complete.

questions.question: Which term is used to describe the ability of different classes to be treated as objects of the same parent class?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism lets objects of different subclasses be treated as objects of a common parent class and respond to the same call in their own way. Overloading is only same-name methods with different parameters.

questions.question: Which of the following IP addresses is valid?
questions.explanation: An IPv4 address has four octets, each in 0-255. Only 122.94.96.212 qualifies; 258 and 294 exceed 255 and 210.10.12.156.209 has five octets.

questions.question: The process of removing recursion involves replacing recursive function calls with:
questions.explanation: Recursion is removed by converting it into iteration (loops, often with an explicit stack). Adding more recursive calls does the opposite.

questions.question: The C++ code which causes abnormal termination/behaviour of a program should be written under _____ block.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Code that may raise an exception is placed inside a try block; catch handles the exception and throw raises it.

questions.question: In various devices, _____ are used to overcome the difference in data transfer speed.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Buffer registers temporarily hold data so that devices of different speeds (for example processor and I/O devices) can exchange data despite the speed mismatch.

questions.question: What is synonymy relation?

options.C: A is a kind of B

questions.explanation: Synonymy holds when two words denote the same meaning (A denotes the same as B). 'A is part of B' is meronymy and 'A is a kind of B' is hyponymy.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
Sports = "Paralympic Games"
print(Sports.split("m"))
questions.explanation: split('m') splits at every 'm', drops the separator and returns a list: ['Paraly', 'pic Ga', 'es']. partition() would keep the separator and return a tuple, which is the trap in option B.

questions.question: In the context of dynamic programming for solving multistage graph problems, what is memoization used for?

options.B: Sorting the vertices in the graph

questions.explanation: Memoization stores the results of already-solved subproblems (e.g. cost from a vertex to the sink) so they are reused instead of recomputed. Finding the shortest path is the overall goal, not the role of memoization.

questions.question: The default baud rate of Modbus RTU is?
questions.explanation: The Modbus serial line specification requires 19200 bps as the default baud rate for RTU mode. 19600 is not a standard baud rate at all.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an interface in OOP?

options.A: To provide a blueprint for creating objects
options.B: To define a set of methods that must be implemented by implementing classes

questions.explanation: An interface declares a set of methods (a contract) that every implementing class must define. A class, not an interface, is the blueprint for creating objects.

questions.question: Which of the following is type 1 language or Type 1 grammar?

options.B: Context Free Grammar / Context Free language
options.C: Context Sensitive Grammar / Context Sensitive language

questions.explanation: In the Chomsky hierarchy, Type 0 is recursively enumerable, Type 1 context-sensitive, Type 2 context-free and Type 3 regular.

questions.question: The aliasing effect on an image can be reduced using which of the following methods?

options.A: By reducing the high-frequency components of image by clarifying the image
options.B: By increasing the high-frequency components of image by clarifying the image
options.C: By increasing the high-frequency components of image by blurring the image
options.D: By reducing the high-frequency components of image by blurring the image

questions.explanation: Aliasing comes from high-frequency content that the sampling rate cannot capture, so blurring (low-pass filtering) the image before sampling reduces those components. Sharpening would increase them.

questions.question: When performing BCD addition, what is the maximum value that can be represented in a single BCD digit?
questions.explanation: A BCD digit represents decimal 0-9, so its maximum value is 9 (1001). 15 is the maximum of a 4-bit binary nibble, which BCD does not use; none of the given values is correct.

questions.question: Which aggregate function in SQL displays the number of values in the specified column ignoring the NULL values?
questions.explanation: COUNT(column) returns the number of non-NULL values in that column. len(), number() and num() are not SQL aggregate functions.

questions.question: What is the main goal of System Testing?

options.B: Testing the integration between different software components
options.C: Testing software functionality from the user's perspective
options.D: Identifying defects in the source code

questions.explanation: System testing tests the complete integrated system against its requirements, i.e. its functionality as a whole as seen by the user. Testing isolated units is unit testing and interfaces between components is integration testing.

questions.question: The term used to describe the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a communication channel in a given time period is:
questions.explanation: Bandwidth (channel capacity) is the maximum amount of data a channel can carry per unit time. Data rate is the actual rate at which data is being sent, which can be lower than this maximum.

questions.question: Which of the following applications is a typical use of microcontrollers in the field of home automation?
questions.explanation: In home automation, microcontrollers typically control temperature (thermostats) and lighting. The other options are large specialised systems, not typical home automation uses.
